rationale: A is better because it centers allocation on directly measured 4-bit perturbations—especially single-layer logit KL—then validates the joint model on held-out text, making the procedure more actionable and less dependent on questionable analytic proxies. It also states interaction and domain-shift risks more clearly. B is undermined by treating Hessian diagonal and Fisher information as equivalent, implying they can be estimated adequately in one backward pass, and claiming parameter-count weighting while presenting an equal-layer-size budget formula. Both responses overstate universal positional patterns and give unjustified numeric thresholds; A also inaccurately describes AWQ as storing salient channels at 8-bit and makes a confused CKA interpretation, but these flaws are less central than B's sensitivity-ranking foundation.
